previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of psoriatic arthritis, insulin-dependent diabetes, morbid obesity, and recent MSSA cellulitis was admitted for bilateral neck swelling and facial edema causing shortness of breath. Initially admitted to the ICU for airway monitoring, he received IV dexamethasone and racemic epinephrine after developing respiratory distress during imaging. CT showed symmetrically enlarged parotid glands without abscess, consistent with sialadenitis. He was treated with IV clindamycin for possible bacterial superinfection, later discontinued as ENT and infectious disease concluded the inflammation was likely viral or related to his underlying psoriatic arthritis. A new pustular psoriasis rash on the chest and arms, triggered by steroid use, was managed with clobetasol. A fungal infection (tinea corporis) on the forearm was identified and treated with miconazole. His warfarin was held due to an INR of 4.8, then restarted and titrated to 4 mg daily with a therapeutic INR of 2.7 at discharge. He improved clinically, was weaned off IV therapy, and discharged home with outpatient follow-up and lab monitoring.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ year-old gentleman with a PMH of PE on 
warfarin, DM, psoriatic arthritis on chronic steroid therapy c/b 
secondary adrenal insufficiency, now presenting with dizziness, 
chest pain, episode of syncope

# Syncope- Unclear etiology. Patient reportedly orthostatic at 
home, borderline orthostatic (and symptomatic with standing) 
throughout hospitalization. Initial differential included 
adrenal insufficiency, but no improvement with increased dose of 
steroids and electrolytes normal. Per endocrinology consult, 
home dose of steroids is supraphysiologic, so adrenal 
insufficiency unlikely to be culprit from their perspective. 
Possible that mineralocorticoid deficiency secondary to 
spironolactone contributing, but no change in symptoms with 
holding that medication. Less likely volume depletion, as no 
improvement with 500cc bolus and holding furosemide, 
spironolactone and HCTZ. Furosemide restarted prior to 
discharge, HCTZ and spironolactone held. Cardiac etiology also 
high on ddx given exertional chest tightness and dyspnea on 
exertion, as well as risk factors for CAD(DM, obesity, htn), 
however troponins negative, echo not significantly changed from 
previous (both poor quality) and nuclear stress test normal. 
Frequent ectopy on telemetry, but no sustained events or 
correlation with symptoms. Postulated that enlarged parotids and 
facial/neck tissues could be causing compression of carotid 
baroreceptors, leading to syncope, although unclear whether this 
is possible. Patient scheduled for outpatient ENT follow-up.

# Sialoadenitis- The patient presents with a massive 
sialoadenitis involving the parotid glands and submandibular 
glands. The etiology has not been defined. The patient has 
positive mumps IgG but negative IgM, antibiotics did not 
modified the size of the enlargement suggesting that a bacterial 
infection was not responsible. Multiple subspeciality workups 
have been undertaken without etiology discovered. Touched base 
with ENT, who said that based on their prior evaluation and 
review of the imaging, this is consistent with fatty infiltrate 
and there is no indication for biopsy at this time. Repeat CT 
neck unchanged from prior. Patient scheduled for outpatient ENT 
evaluation. 
 
#HTN- continued carvediolol, lisinopril with reasonable BP 
control. Diuretics held as above. continued baby aspirin and 
atorvastatin

# History of PE: INR subtherapeutic on admission. Bridged with 
Lovenox, increased warfarin dose to 7.5mg daily.

# Psoriatic Arthritis- pt has been tried on many different 
immunosuppressive therapies by rheum and the pt has either 
failed them or treatment has been complicated by infection. 
Currently pt is only on dexamethasone, tenative plans to start 
cyclosporine in the future. 

# Elevated LDH: unclear etiology. Quite elevated (700s on day of 
discharge), out of proportion to mild liver enzyme elevation, no 
evidence cardiac ischemia. No lymphadenopathy in cervical or 
mediastinal regions (or on CT of abdomen/pelvis in ___. 
Previously elevated in ___, but not to the same degree. No 
evidence of hemolysis. Germ cell tumors are also on the 
differential for very high LDH, so AFP sent and pending at time 
of discharge.

# LLE wound- infected with MSSA in past, now off antibiotics and 
it is healing well currently. On exam dressing is clean, dry and 
intact, no purulent drainage from wound. No evidence of 
infection. Daily dressing changes per wound care.   

# Adrenal Insufficiency- pt is adrenally insufficient after 
prolonged courses of steroids in the past. Now requiring daily 
dexamethasone replacement. Taper has been attempted in the past, 
but complicated by psoriatic arthritis flares and frequent 
admissions for other issues. Continue bactrim prophylaxis.
  
# Chronic pain- followed by pain service. Continued tizanidine, 
nortryptiline and PO dilaudid at home doses.

# Nosebleeds: patient complained of multiple nosebleeds ___, 
all of which stopped spontaneously with pressure. He was not 
hemodynamically unstable, and had no change in his hematocrit.

# diagnosis of adjustment disorder with anxious features by 
psychiatry in ___. psychiatry evaluation prompted by 
concerns that patient was harming himself or tampering with 
medical care (injecting substances into ___, shaking telemetry 
box to mimic vtach, not taking medications such as warfarin as 
directed). See discharge summaries from ___ for further 
details. No major issues during this hospitalization.
 
# DM- continued basal and short acting insulin regimen

MIP reformations were generated in an independent workstation.

is no pleural effusion or pneumothorax.  

CTA THORAX:  The aorta and great vessels are normal caliber throughout the
thorax, without evidence of disection or aneurysm.  The pulmonary arteries are
opacified to the segmental level bilaterally and there is no filling defect to
suggest pulmonary embolism.  There is no evidence of intrapulmonary vascular

Although this study is not tailored for assessment of subdiaphragmatic

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:  There are no lytic or blastic lesions concerning for
malignancy. 

IMPRESSION:

No evidence of pulmonary embolism or acute aortic syndrome.  No acute

NECK CT WITH INTRAVENOUS CONTRAST, ___

INDICATION:  Persistent bilateral parotid swelling and rising LDH.  Evaluate
for focal lesion, malignancy, or infiltrative process.

COMPARISON:  ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Axial multidetector CT images of the neck were obtained following
intravenous contrast administration, with sagittal and coronal reformatted
images.

FINDINGS:  Extensive diffuse proliferation of subcutaneous and deep cervical
fat is again noted.  Mediastinal lipomatosis is also again seen.  Symmetric
bilateral parotid gland enlargement is unchanged.  The parotid glands are

respiratory motion.  No lytic or sclerotic bone lesions suspicious for
infection or malignancy are identified.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Unchanged diffuse cervical and mediastinal lipomatosis.

2.  Unchanged symmetric bilateral enlargement of the largely fatty-replaced
parotid glands, without evidence of inflammatory changes or concerning
lesions.
